proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\mathcal O\) for the relative interior of the attainable support.  In a topological ordering of \(G_0\), the triangular change of variables
\[
 T(v)_j=v_j-f_j(v_{\operatorname{pa}_0(j)})
\]
has triangular Jacobian with diagonal entries one.  Hence Assumption \(\ref{ass:anm-independence}\), the structural equations in Definition \(\ref{def:base-model}\), and the change-of-variables formula give, almost everywhere on \(\mathcal X\),
\[
 p_P(v)=\prod_{j\in I}p_{N_j}\!\left(v_j-f_j(v_{\operatorname{pa}_0(j)})\right)
 =p_{f,p_N}(v).
\]
Assumption \(\ref{ass:support-closure}\) makes this a probability density supported on \(\mathcal X\), rather than a formal recursion which can leave the recorded node ranges.  Because every innovation has a density, every boundary face of an innovation interval, and hence its inverse image under \(T\), has \(P\)-measure zero.

Fix one of the conditioning configurations in Assumption \(\ref{ass:condition19-configurations}\).  Conditioning the displayed product density and cancelling its normalizing constant shows that the conditional density on a nonempty fiber is a quotient of finite products of the factors in Definition \(\ref{def:structural-density}\).  Assumptions \(\ref{ass:smooth-mechanisms}\) and \(\ref{ass:smooth-positive-densities}\) therefore make that density strictly positive and three times continuously differentiable on the fiber's relative interior.  Assumption \(\ref{ass:connected-support-fibers}\) makes that relative interior connected.  In particular, an almost-everywhere conditional factorization on the fiber extends, by continuity, throughout each open coordinate patch.  On two overlapping patches the two extensions agree on a nonempty open overlap; connectedness then propagates the same factorization along a finite chain of overlapping patches.  Thus distinct reverse factorizations cannot be pasted on disconnected pieces.  Since the omitted boundary is null, all conditional-independence equalities required by the restricted-ANM argument hold under the original conditional law.

We now invoke the finite-graph reduction and bivariate differential obstruction in Lemma \(\ref{lem:peters-restricted-anm-identification}\).  Its proof uses positivity only to obtain the preceding intersection-and-localization step.  We have just established that step on every relevant relative interior.  If a second causally minimal additive-noise DAG generated \(P\), the reduction would produce an edge \(u\to v\), a set \(A\) with
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_0(v)\setminus\{u\}\subseteq A
 \subseteq\operatorname{nd}_0(v)\setminus\{u,v\},
\]
and a positive-density conditional section on which both causal directions admitted additive-noise representations.  The bivariate part of the cited lemma then forces Peters et al.'s differential equation (7) on every open subpatch on which its denominators are nonzero.  Assumption \(\ref{ass:condition19-configurations}\) supplies, for this same \((u,v,A)\), an interior open subpatch on which that equation fails.  This is a contradiction.  Assumption \(\ref{ass:causal-minimality}\) rules out removal of a true edge before the reduction is applied.  Therefore no distinct causally minimal additive-noise DAG generates \(P\), so the observed law \(P\) identifies the labelled graph \(G_0\).

Fix \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\).  Independence of the innovations and the matching-component condition imply that the random vectors belonging to distinct weak components of \(G_0\) are mutually independent.  Consider an edge component \(u\to v\).  For any set \(B\) made only of nodes in other components, conditional expectation and independence give
\[
 q(v,B)=q(u,B)=0,
\]
\[
 q(v,B\cup\{u\})
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}\{f_v(V_u)\}}
 {\operatorname{Var}\{f_v(V_u)\}+\operatorname{Var}(N_v)}
 =\rho^{\to}_{uv},
\]
and
\[
 q(u,B\cup\{v\})
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}\{\mathbb E[V_u\mid V_v]\}}
 {\operatorname{Var}(V_u)}
 =\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}.
\]
The divisions are valid by Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\), which is a member property of \(\mathcal M_0(d)\).

When \(u\) precedes \(v\), the residual after regressing \(V_v\) on \(B\cup\{u\}\) is \(N_v-\mathbb E N_v\).  It is independent of every predecessor by Assumption \(\ref{ass:anm-independence}\), so characteristicness in Definition \(\ref{def:hsic}\) gives \(D(v,B\cup\{u\})=0\).  Thus the edge component contributes \(\rho^{\to}_{uv}\) to \(S_P\).  When \(v\) precedes \(u\), regression on \(B\cup\{v\}\) is the same as regression on \(V_v\).  If its residual were independent of \(V_v\), it would give the reverse additive-noise representation
\[
 V_u=\mathbb E[V_u\mid V_v]+E,
 \qquad E\perp V_v.
\]
The Condition 19 configuration and Lemma \(\ref{lem:compact-identifiability}\) exclude that representation.  The residual is independent of every member of \(B\), however, because \((V_u,V_v)\) is independent of the other components.  Therefore, if \(a=|B|+1\) is the number of predecessors of \(u\),
\[
 D(u,B\cup\{v\})=1,
 \qquad
 \ell_P(u,B\cup\{v\})
 =\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}\frac{a}{a+1}
 \le \frac{d-1}{d}\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}.
\]

Let \(\pi\notin\Pi(G_0)\).  Some edge component \(u\to v\) is reversed in \(\pi\).  Move \(u\) from its rank to the rank immediately before \(v\).  Since \(u\) has no descendant other than \(v\), this removes the ancestral reversal \((u,v)\) and creates none, so the move belongs to \(\operatorname{Corr}_{G_0}(\pi)\).  The contribution of this component changes from at most \((d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\) to \(\rho^{\to}_{uv}\).  For each node \(w\) strictly traversed by the insertion, the new predecessor set is its old predecessor set with the independent variable \(V_u\) added.  Its conditional mean, explained risk, and dependence count are unchanged, while
\[
 1-\frac{D(w,A)}{|A|+2}\ge 1-\frac{D(w,A)}{|A|+1}.
\]
All other local terms are unchanged.  Definitions \(\ref{def:gene-score}\) and \(\ref{def:insertion-gain}\) consequently yield
\[
 C_P(\pi;r,s)
 \ge \rho^{\to}_{uv}-\frac{d-1}{d}\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}
 \ge\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}>0,
\]
where strict positivity follows from Assumption \(\ref{ass:pair-signal-dominance}\) and finiteness of the edge set.  (If the graph has no edges, every order is topological and the assertion about non-topological orders is vacuous.)  Finally, an insertion-local maximizer cannot be non-topological, because the construction above would supply a strictly improving insertion.  Hence every insertion-local maximizer is topological.

First write the global reversal-monotone premise used by Li et al. in the form
\[
 \operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi)<\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi')
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad S_P(\pi)>S_P(\pi').
\]
On a matching graph, every non-topological order has the correcting insertion constructed in Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\), and that insertion strictly decreases \(\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}\).  The displayed premise therefore implies the positive correcting-move property.

We prove failure of the converse using Definition \(\ref{def:li-separation-witness}\).  The three edge components are independent.  All displayed root and innovation densities are positive and \(C^3\) on their relative interiors; the mechanisms are \(C^3\), nonconstant, and their stated node intervals contain the structural outputs.  Variances are positive.  The relevant conditional fibers for the root given variables from the other components have connected interiors.  It remains to verify the differential obstruction.  If \(\xi=\log p_X\), \(\nu=\log p_N\), \(t=y-f(x)\), and
\[
 L(x,y)=\xi(x)+\nu(t),
\]
then a reverse additive-noise representation implies, wherever \(L_{xx}\ne0\),
\[
 \partial_x\!\left(\frac{L_{xy}}{L_{xx}}\right)=0. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, in a reverse representation \(L(x,y)=\widetilde\nu(x-g(y))+\widetilde\xi(y)\), and the ratio is \(-g'(y)\).  For the symmetric bump innovation, at \(t=0\) one has \(\nu'(0)=\nu'''(0)=0\) and \(\nu''(0)<0\).  For the cosine edge, at \(x=1/2\), \(f'(x)=0\), \(f''(x)=4\pi^2\), and \(\xi''(x)\ne0\), so the left side of (1) equals
\[
 -\frac{f''(x)\nu''(0)}{\xi''(x)}\ne0.
\]
For either quadratic edge, substitution at \(t=0\) reduces the numerator in (1), up to the nonzero factor \(\nu''(0)\), to
\[
 f'(x)\xi'''(x)-f''(x)\xi''(x)+2f'(x)^2f''(x)\nu''(0). \tag{2}
\]
For \(f(x)=x+x^2\) and \(\xi(x)=-1/[x(1-x)]+\mathrm{constant}\), the quotient
\[
 \frac{f'(x)\xi'''(x)-f''(x)\xi''(x)}{2f'(x)^2f''(x)}
\]
is not constant on \((0,1)\) (direct differentiation gives a nonzero rational function).  Hence (2) cannot vanish for every \(x\) for any fixed value \(\nu''(0)=-2/\sigma^2\).  For every \(\sigma>0\) there is therefore an interior point where (1) fails, and continuity makes the failure hold on an open patch.  Thus Assumption \(\ref{ass:condition19-configurations}\) holds; Lemma \(\ref{lem:compact-identifiability}\) gives identifiability, and the witness belongs to \(\mathcal M_0(6)\).

For edge \(1\to2\), symmetry under \(x\mapsto1-x\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E[V_1\mid V_2]=\frac12,
 \qquad \rho^{\leftarrow}_{12}=0,
\]
whereas
\[
 \rho^{\to}_{12}
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}\{\cos(2\pi V_1)\}}
 {\operatorname{Var}\{\cos(2\pi V_1)\}+\sigma^2\operatorname{Var}(Z_2)}
 \longrightarrow1.
\]
For \(h(x)=x+x^2\), the inverse of \(h\) on \([0,1]\) is one-Lipschitz.  Extending it by clipping to \([0,1]\) gives an estimator \(\widetilde X(V)=h^{-1}_{\mathrm{clip}}(V)\) satisfying
\[
 \mathbb E\{(X-\widetilde X(h(X)+\sigma Z))^2\}
 \le \sigma^2\mathbb E[Z^2].
\]
The conditional mean minimizes squared risk, so the conditional-variance identity gives
\[
 1-\rho^{\leftarrow}
 =\frac{\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(X\mid h(X)+\sigma Z)}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
 \le\frac{\sigma^2\mathbb E[Z^2]}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The forward ratio is \(\operatorname{Var}(h(X))/\{\operatorname{Var}(h(X))+\sigma^2\operatorname{Var}(Z)\}\to1\).  Consequently both directional ratios on edges \(3\to4\) and \(5\to6\) tend to one.  Since their pairwise gaps tend to \(1-5/6=1/6\), and the cosine gap tends to one, Assumption \(\ref{ass:pair-signal-dominance}\) holds for all sufficiently small positive \(\sigma\).  Hence \(P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(6)\).

The local score calculation in the proof of Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) now gives the score limits exactly.  In \(\pi_1=(2,3,4,5,6,1)\), the cosine edge is reversed but has reverse ratio zero, while the other two edges are forward, so
\[
 S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_1)\longrightarrow 0+1+1=2.
\]
In \(\pi_2=(1,2,4,6,3,5)\), the cosine edge is forward.  The roots of the two reversed quadratic edges have respectively four and five predecessors; their reverse residuals are dependent on their effects by (1), and independent of all variables in the other components.  Thus
\[
 S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_2)\longrightarrow
 1+\frac45+\frac56>2.
\]
Direct counting gives \(\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_1)=1<2=\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_2)\).  The ratios above are continuous in \(\sigma>0\), and the dependence indicators stay equal to one because (1) fails for every sufficiently small positive \(\sigma\).  The reverse score inequality is therefore strict for all sufficiently small \(\sigma\), contradicting global reversal monotonicity.  Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) nevertheless supplies the local recovery guarantee.

Let \(h(x)=x+x^2\) and \(m_2=\mathbb E[Z^2]\).  Since \(Z\) is symmetric, \(\mathbb E Z=0\), and Definition \(\ref{def:positive-witness}\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E[Y\mid X]=h(X),\qquad
 \varepsilon_{Y,\{X\}}=\sigma Z,
\]
so the forward residual is independent of \(X\).  Moreover
\[
 q(Y,\{X\})
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}(h(X))}
 {\operatorname{Var}(h(X))+\sigma^2m_2}
 \ge 1-\frac{\sigma^2m_2}{\operatorname{Var}(h(X))}. \tag{2}
\]
The denominator is positive because \(h\) is nonconstant under the uniform law.

We next show that \(\varepsilon_{X,\{Y\}}=X-\mathbb E[X\mid Y]\) is not independent of \(Y\).  Positivity of both densities on their support interiors gives, for every \(y\in(-\sigma,\sigma)\),
\[
 \operatorname{supp}(X\mid Y=y)^{\circ}
 =\bigl(0,h^{-1}(y+\sigma)\bigr).
\]
Translation by \(-\mathbb E[X\mid Y=y]\) does not change the diameter of this interval.  Its diameter \(h^{-1}(y+\sigma)\) is strictly increasing in \(y\) on an interval having positive \(P_Y\)-density.  If the residual were independent of \(Y\), its conditional support would agree with one fixed marginal support for almost every such \(y\), which is impossible because these diameters differ.  Hence characteristicness of the kernel implies \(H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0\).

For two nodes, the correct order has score \(q(Y,\{X\})\), while the wrong order has score \(q(X,\{Y\})/2\): the factor is one half because the reverse residual has exactly one dependent predecessor.  Therefore
\[
 C_{P_{\mathrm w,\sigma}}((Y,X);2,1)
 =q(Y,\{X\})-\frac12q(X,\{Y\})
 \ge q(Y,\{X\})-\frac12
 \ge\frac12-\frac{\sigma^2m_2}{\operatorname{Var}(X+X^2)},
\]
where \(q(X,\{Y\})\le1\) follows from the conditional-variance decomposition.  This lower bound is positive for sufficiently small \(\sigma\).  The one-Lipschitz inverse argument used in the proof of Theorem \(\ref{thm:li-strict-separation}\) gives \(q(X,\{Y\})\to1\), while (2) gives \(q(Y,\{X\})\to1\), so the gain converges to \(1/2\).

Finally, \(h([0,1])+[-\sigma,\sigma]\subseteq[-\sigma,2+\sigma]\), proving support closure.  To check the differential premise explicitly, put \(L(x,y)=\log p_X(x)+\log p_{\sigma Z}(y-h(x))\).  At any interior point with \(y=h(x)\), the uniform root has zero log-density derivatives, while the symmetric bump has \(\nu'(0)=\nu'''(0)=0\) and \(\nu''(0)<0\).  Direct differentiation yields
\[
 \partial_x\!\left(\frac{L_{xy}}{L_{xx}}\right)
 =\frac{2h''(x)}{h'(x)^2}=\frac{4}{(1+2x)^2}\ne0.
\]
A reverse additive-noise representation would make this ratio a function of \(y\) alone.  Thus Peters et al.'s differential identity fails on an interior open set by continuity, verifying the stated Condition 19 requirement.

Run the map in Definition \(\ref{def:oracle-recovery}\) from an arbitrary \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_I\).  Every accepted insertion has strictly positive gain, so \(S_P\) strictly increases.  An order can therefore never be revisited.  Since \(|\mathfrak S_I|=d!\), at most \(d!-1\) insertions are accepted.  If the terminal order were non-topological, Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) would provide a positive correcting insertion, contradicting termination.  Thus the terminal order is topological.

It remains to verify pruning.  In a topological order on a matching graph, a nonparent predecessor \(u\) of \(v\) lies in another independent component.  As long as the current ordered parent set \(A\) contains the true parent when one exists,
\[
 \mathbb E[V_v\mid V_{A\setminus\{u\}}]
 =\mathbb E[V_v\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}_0(v)}],
\]
and its residual is a centered innovation, independent of \(V_u\).  Hence \(H(v,A\setminus\{u\},u)=0\), and every nonedge is deleted.  If \(u\) is the true parent of \(v\), all variables in \(A\setminus\{u\}\) are from independent components, so the tested residual is \(V_v-\mathbb E V_v\).  Were it independent of \(V_u\), the pair would admit both the stated nonconstant forward ANM and an independence factorization, contrary to causal minimality and the Condition 19 identification conclusion in Lemma \(\ref{lem:compact-identifiability}\).  Characteristicness therefore gives \(H(v,A\setminus\{u\},u)>0\), so no true edge is deleted.  This invariant also shows that the conclusion is independent of the deletion order.  The output is exactly \(G_0\).

There are \(d(d-1)\) ordered insertions at each visited order, including the terminal order.  At most \(d!\) orders are visited, giving at most \(d(d-1)d!\) gain comparisons.  Every score is determined by the table
\[
 \{R_{v,A}:v\in I,\ A\subseteq I\setminus\{v\}\},
\]
which has \(d2^{d-1}\) entries, and the score-relevant table
\[
 \{H(v,A,u):v\in I,\ A\subseteq I\setminus\{v\},\ u\in A\},
\]
which has
\[
 d(d-1)2^{d-2}
\]
entries.  Memoization therefore gives the asserted risk and score-HSIC query bounds.  A complete ordered DAG has at most \(d(d-1)/2\) arrows, so pruning requires at most that many additional HSIC checks.

All coordinates and all residuals are bounded because \(\mathcal X\) is compact.  We first record a regression construction.  If \(|A|=m\le d-1\), partition the compact rectangle \(\mathcal X_A\) into cubes of side \(h\) and use, on each cube, polynomials of total degree two, clipped to the outcome range.  Taylor's formula and Assumption \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\) give a sieve element \(g_h\) with
\[
 \|g_h-\mu_{v,A}\|_\infty\le K_0h^3,
\]
while the sieve dimension is at most \(K_1h^{-m}\).  For bounded squared loss, the basic inequality for empirical least squares, followed by Bernstein's inequality on a Euclidean net of this finite-dimensional clipped sieve, gives, conditionally on a training fold and with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[
 \|\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\|_{L^2(P_A)}^2
 \le K_2\left\{h^6+\frac{h^{-m}\log(L/\delta)}{n}\right\}. \tag{10}
\]
Here \(L\) is the number of regressions fitted simultaneously; the density bounds ensure that the same constants work on nonempty design cells, while empty cells carry no \(P_A\)-risk.  To see the fast rather than square-root stochastic term in (10), apply Bernstein to the loss difference: its variance is bounded by a constant times its mean excess risk because the responses and candidates are bounded.  Peeling the net by excess-risk shells and summing the resulting geometric probabilities proves (10).

Choose \(h=\{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\}^{1/(m+6)}\), use the largest dimension \(m=d-1\), and absorb fold-size constants into \(K\).  A union bound over the \(d2^{d-1}\) regressions yields
\[
 \max_{v,A}\|\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\|_{L^2(P_A)}
 \le K a_n. \tag{11}
\]
For the finitely many small \(n\) for which the chosen sieve has fewer than one effective cell, clipping and a larger \(K\) give the same inequality.

On a held-out fold, define \(\widehat R_{v,A}\) as the average squared residual formed with the off-fold fit.  Conditional on that fit, orthogonality of conditional expectation gives
\[
 \mathbb E[(V_v-\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A))^2\mid\widehat\mu_{v,A}]
 =R_{v,A}+\|\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\|_{L^2(P_A)}^2. \tag{12}
\]
Hoeffding's inequality for bounded held-out losses, a union bound, (11), and (12) produce simultaneous intervals containing every \(R_{v,A}\) with half-width
\[
 w_R\le K\left\{\sqrt{\frac{\log(M_d/\alpha)}n}+a_n^2\right\}. \tag{13}
\]

Next compute bounded-kernel HSIC as its usual centered order-four V-statistic on a held-out fold.  Replacing one held-out observation changes it by at most \(K/n\), so the bounded-difference inequality and a union bound give fluctuation at most \(K\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}\).  Its diagonal V-statistic bias is \(O(n^{-1})\), which is absorbed by this term.  If \(e_i\) and \(\widehat e_i\) are the true and fitted residuals, Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\), telescoping the finite product of kernel factors, and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 |\operatorname{HSIC}(\widehat e,V_u)-\operatorname{HSIC}(e,V_u)|
 \le K\mathbb E|\widehat e-e|
 \le K\|\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\|_{L^2(P_A)}.
\]
Together with (11), this gives simultaneous score-relevant HSIC bands with
\[
 w_H\le K\left\{\sqrt{\frac{\log(M_d/\alpha)}n}+a_n\right\}. \tag{14}
\]
The same construction is made for the pruning functionals \(H(v,A,u)\) with \(u\notin A\).  There are at most another \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) of them; replacing \(M_d\) by at most \(2M_d\) changes only the universal multiplicative constant in (13)--(14), since \(\log(2M_d/\alpha)\le2\log(M_d/\alpha)\).  Thus every adaptively queried pruning value is covered on the same event.

Suppose now that all queried HSIC values lie in \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\) and \(2w_H<\lambda\).  If the true value is zero, coverage implies that the interval's upper endpoint is below \(\lambda\); if it is at least \(\lambda\), the lower endpoint is strictly positive.  Hence every set-valued decision is the correct singleton.  In particular, the discontinuous indicator is used only after separation; when an interval meets both regions Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\) retains both labels.

Under singleton dependence decisions, interval arithmetic applied to Definitions \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\)--\(\ref{def:insertion-gain}\) contains every true gain, because Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\) keeps all variance denominators away from zero.  At any non-topological order, Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) supplies a correcting gain at least \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\).  Every score table compatible with the bands assigns that same gain a value at least \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}-2w_S>0\).  Strict ascent on the finite permutation set therefore makes every compatible terminal order topological.  The singleton pruning decisions are exactly those in Theorem \(\ref{thm:oracle-recovery}\), so every compatible terminal DAG equals \(G_0\).  Their union is \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\).

If a band meets both \(0\) and \([\lambda,\infty)\), the construction records both labels (and also does so after an empty intersection), so it never converts proximity to the discontinuity into a false binary assertion.  Taking the union over all compatible paths proves the final, deliberately set-valued conclusion.  Such a union can still be a singleton if the ambiguous functional is irrelevant to every terminal pruning decision; therefore no unconditional multiplicity claim is made.

theorem.statement:
There is an explicitly parameterized nonempty relatively open subset \(\mathcal U\subset\mathcal M_0(2)\) and one may take \(\eta=1/5\) such that every law in \(\mathcal U\) satisfies
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})\ge\eta,
 \qquad H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0.
\]
Consequently the noncausal order \((Y,X)\) is a strict insertion-local maximizer of the exact \(\alpha=1\) population GENE score throughout \(\mathcal U\), although every law in \(\mathcal U\) identifies the causal order \(X\to Y\).
theorem.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 b(z)=c_b\exp\{-1/(1-z^2)\}\mathbf 1\{|z|<1\},
 \qquad m_2=\int z^2b(z)\,dz,
\]
and let \(\beta(t)=c_\beta\exp\{-1/[t(1-t)]\}\mathbf 1\{0<t<1\}\).  Put \(L=3\), \(\epsilon_\star=m_2/72\), and
\[
 v_\star=L^2\epsilon_\star(1-\epsilon_\star)>0.
\]
For \(0<h<1/2\) and \(0<\tau<1\), define on \([0,L]\)
\[
 p_{h,\tau}(x)
 =(1-\tau)\left\{(1-\epsilon_\star)h^{-1}\beta(x/h)
 +\epsilon_\star h^{-1}\beta((L-x)/h)\right\}+\frac{\tau}{L}. \tag{3}
\]
Terms involving \(\beta\) are understood as zero outside their displayed endpoint intervals.  Take \(X\) to have density (3), take \(N\) to have density \(b\), independently, and set \(Y=X+N\), with node domains \([0,3]\) and \([-1,4]\).

The densities in (3) and \(b\) are strictly positive and \(C^3\) on their relative interiors, the mechanism is smooth and nonconstant, and support closure is immediate.  The root support is connected.  To verify Condition 19, write \(\xi=\log p_{h,\tau}\), \(\nu=\log b\), and \(L_0(x,y)=\xi(x)+\nu(y-x)\).  A reverse ANM would force
\[
 \partial_x\{(L_0)_{xy}/(L_0)_{xx}\}=0. \tag{4}
\]
At \(y=x\), where \(\nu'''(0)=0\), the left side of (4) is nonzero at any point for which \(\xi'''(x)\ne0\) and \(\xi''(x)+\nu''(0)\ne0\).  Such a point exists: \(p_{h,\tau}\) is constant on \((h,L-h)\) but nonconstant on an endpoint interval, so \(\xi'''\) cannot vanish identically; and \(\xi''=-\nu''(0)\) cannot hold on every open set on which \(\xi'''\ne0\).  Continuity gives failure on an open patch.  Thus these laws satisfy all member properties of \(\mathcal M_0(2)\), including its Condition 19 restriction, and Lemma \(\ref{lem:compact-identifiability}\) identifies \(X\to Y\).

Couple \(X\) to \(X_0\in\{0,L\}\), with \(P(X_0=L)=\epsilon_\star\), by using the corresponding endpoint label on the first mixture term in (3), and any coupling on the bridge term.  Then
\[
 \mathbb E(X-X_0)^2\le B_{h,\tau}:=h^2+L^2\tau. \tag{5}
\]
The reverse triangle inequality in \(L^2\), applied after centering, gives
\[
 \left|\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(X)}-\sqrt{v_\star}\right|
 \le2\sqrt{B_{h,\tau}},
\]
and therefore \(|\operatorname{Var}(X)-v_\star|\le12\sqrt{B_{h,\tau}}\), since both variables lie in \([0,3]\).  Choose explicit positive \(h,\tau\) satisfying
\[
 B_{h,\tau}<\min\{v_\star/10,\ v_\star^2/2304\}. \tag{6}
\]
Then
\[
 \frac34v_\star<\operatorname{Var}(X)<\frac54v_\star.
\]
Because \(v_\star<m_2/8\), the forward correlation ratio obeys
\[
 q(Y,\{X\})
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{\operatorname{Var}(X)+m_2}
 <\frac15. \tag{7}
\]

For \(h<1/2\), the estimator \(\widehat X(Y)=0\) when \(Y<3/2\) and \(\widehat X(Y)=3\) otherwise classifies both endpoint components correctly.  Its squared error is at most \(h^2\) on those components and at most \(9\) on the bridge.  By conditional-mean optimality, (5)--(6) imply
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)
 \le B_{h,\tau},
 \qquad
 q(X,\{Y\})
 =1-\frac{\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
 >\frac{13}{15}. \tag{8}
\]
Combining (7) and (8) yields
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})
 >\frac{13}{30}-\frac15=\frac7{30}>\frac15. \tag{9}
\]

The reverse residual is dependent on \(Y\) for a support-geometric reason which is stable under perturbation.  At the displayed law,
\[
 \operatorname{supp}(X\mid Y=y)^{\circ}
 =\bigl(\max\{0,y-1\},\min\{3,y+1\}\bigr).
\]
On \(y\in(-1,1)\) its diameter is \(y+1\), which is not constant on a set of positive \(P_Y\)-measure.  Centering by \(\mathbb E[X\mid Y=y]\) only translates this support.  Independence of the centered residual and \(Y\) would require one common conditional support almost everywhere, a contradiction.  Characteristicness gives \(H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0\).

For completeness, define the structural topology by taking the graph discretely, the support endpoints in their Euclidean topology, mechanisms in \(C^1\), and compactly supported densities in \(L^1\) together with compact-open \(C^3\) convergence on relative interiors.  Around any parameter pair satisfying (6), impose the following strict primitive conditions: the mechanism is strictly increasing; the images of the two endpoint bands remain separated by more than the innovation-support diameter; the root mass outside those bands is small enough that the classifier bound divided by \(\operatorname{Var}(X)\) is less than \(1/5\); and
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Var}\{f(X)\}}
 {\operatorname{Var}\{f(X)\}+\operatorname{Var}(N)}<\frac15.
\]
These are strict inequalities in structural functions, support endpoints, and density integrals, hence define a relatively open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) inside \(\mathcal M_0(2)\).  The same classifier proof gives \(q(X,\{Y\})>4/5\), and the last display gives \(q(Y,\{X\})<1/5\).  Strict monotonicity and full interior positivity make the diameter of the conditional-support interval vary near a support endpoint, so the reverse HSIC remains positive throughout \(\mathcal U\).  Thus (9), with the uniform choice \(\eta=1/5\), holds on \(\mathcal U\).  The independence indicator is not asserted to be continuous at zero: it is locally constant here only because the structural support argument supplies strict dependence.  Finally, the two possible orders have scores \(q(Y,\{X\})\) and \(q(X,\{Y\})/2\), so (9) makes the wrong order the unique insertion-local maximizer.

added_lemmas.statement: For a distribution generated by a causally minimal restricted additive-noise model satisfying the Condition 19 configurations, the generating DAG is identifiable from the observational distribution.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Under Assumptions \(\ref{ass:iid-sampling}\), \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\), \(\ref{ass:design-density}\), \(\ref{ass:characteristic-kernels}\), and \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\), there is \(K<\infty\) such that, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), all \(d2^{d-1}\) risks and all \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC values lie in their cross-fitted bands, with \(w_R\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n^2\}\) and \(w_H\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n\}\). Boundedness of the kernels controls the held-out empirical fluctuation in \(w_H\), while Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\) is used only to convert the cross-fitted residual error into the additive \(a_n\) term. On this event, if \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), every queried HSIC value belongs to \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), and \(2w_H<\lambda\), then \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\). Without the two separation inequalities, interval propagation never forces a binary label for an HSIC interval meeting both \(0\) and \([\lambda,\infty)\): it retains both labels and returns the union of all compatible terminal DAGs, which may be a singleton or may contain multiple graphs.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original final sentence asserted that any failure to separate an HSIC interval necessarily produces more than one terminal graph. An ambiguous score-only functional, or an ambiguity shared by paths that prune to the same graph, need not change the graph union. The valid honest conclusion is that both labels and all compatible terminal DAGs are retained; the resulting set may or may not be a singleton.

proposed.statement: Every law in \(\mathcal M_0(d)\) identifies \(G_0\). Support closure first makes the structural recursion a law on \(\mathcal X\). On every nonempty conditional-support fiber, the induced density is positive and three times continuously differentiable on a connected relative interior. The conditional-independence intersection argument therefore applies on that open set, connectedness rules out patching distinct reverse factorizations across disjoint interior components, and the support boundary is null. Assumption \(\ref{ass:condition19-configurations}\) then supplies an interior open set on which Peters et al.'s differential identity fails, excluding every reversed bivariate conditional ANM. These steps extend their positive-density Condition 19 argument to the stated compact-support regime without assuming uniqueness of the DAG.
proposed.justification: The compact-domain model needs a genuine identification bridge because positivity only on relative interiors is weaker than full-support positivity.
proposed.gap: Peters et al. (2014, Condition 19, Definition 27, and Theorem 28) do not state the support-closed compact-fiber extension.
proposed.consumer: The score analysis can target the labelled DAG using a proved compact restricted-ANM identification result.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the published restricted-ANM identification theorem as the cited leaf used by the compact-support adaptation.

proposed.statement: Let \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\). For every \(\pi\notin\Pi(G_0)\), choose a component edge \(u\to v\) with \(v\) before \(u\) and insert \(u\) immediately before \(v\). This move belongs to \(\operatorname{Corr}_{G_0}(\pi)\) and satisfies \(C_P(\pi;r,s)\ge\rho^{\to}_{uv}-(d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\ge\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}>0\). The bound follows from the structural product law: before the move the reversed root contributes at most \((d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\), after the move the effect contributes \(\rho^{\to}_{uv}\), and every traversed node from another independent component has unchanged explained risk and a weakly larger GENE penalty factor. Consequently every insertion-local maximizer is topological.
proposed.justification: This is the field-level root result: a check on mechanisms and noise laws yields strict local ascent without assuming any ordering of permutation scores.
proposed.gap: Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3) assume a global ranking for every pair of orders with different ancestral-reversal counts and give no structural-function condition implying a correcting insertion.
proposed.consumer: Benchmark designers can certify population success of insertion search directly from each cause--effect module.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Add the variance and characteristic-kernel assumptions used explicitly in the gain calculation and reverse-dependence step.

proposed.statement: Li et al.'s global reversal-monotone premise implies the positive correcting-move property on the matching-component graph class, but the converse fails even for smooth identifiable ANMs. For all sufficiently small \(\sigma>0\), \(P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(6)\): symmetry gives \(\rho^{\leftarrow}_{12}=0\), while \(\rho^{\to}_{12}\to1\) and both directional ratios on edges \(3\to4\) and \(5\to6\) converge to \(1\). Nevertheless, for \(\pi_1=(2,3,4,5,6,1)\) and \(\pi_2=(1,2,4,6,3,5)\), \(\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_1)=1<2=\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_2)\), whereas \(S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_1)\to2\) and \(S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_2)\to1+4/5+5/6>2\). Continuity of the correlation ratios, together with forward residual independence and Condition 19 reverse dependence for every \(\sigma>0\), makes the reversed ranking strict for small positive \(\sigma\). Thus Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) guarantees local recovery for a support-closed smooth law excluded by Li et al.'s premise.
proposed.justification: An explicit score-limit calculation certifies a strict reduction in the recovery hypothesis, rather than a verbal comparison between differently named conditions.
proposed.gap: Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3 and its proof on page 5) establish sufficiency of global reversal monotonicity but do not separate it from the local property their optimizer needs.
proposed.consumer: Users obtain a guarantee for heterogeneous modular systems whose inversion costs cannot be ranked by an unweighted reversal count.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the structural, variance, and conditional-functional nodes used to verify that the explicit six-node law belongs to the base class and to compute its score limits.

proposed.statement: For \(P_{\mathrm w,\sigma}\), the forward residual is independent of \(X\), the reverse conditional-mean residual is dependent on \(Y\), and, with \(m_2=\mathbb E[Z^2]\), \(C_{P_{\mathrm w,\sigma}}((Y,X);2,1)\ge1/2-\sigma^2m_2/\operatorname{Var}(X+X^2)\). Hence the correcting gain is positive for sufficiently small \(\sigma\) and converges to \(1/2\). The support-closure relation holds on \([0,1]\times[-\sigma,2+\sigma]\), and the Condition 19 differential identity fails on an interior open set.
proposed.justification: The witness supplies a quantitative, scale-invariant calibration of the primitive certificate in the smallest graph.
proposed.gap: Reisach et al. (2023, Sections 3 and 5) analyze normalized explained variance but not its combination with exact residual dependence in GENE Equation (6).
proposed.consumer: Implementers obtain an analytic two-node test case whose population gain approaches one half.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare characteristicness, which turns the proved reverse residual dependence into strict positive HSIC.

proposed.statement: If \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), then \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{or}}(P,\pi)=G_0\) for every \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_I\). Strict ascent prevents revisiting an order, and Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) makes every terminal order topological; Condition 19 configurations and causal minimality then make residual-independence pruning delete exactly the nonedges. The search uses at most \(d!-1\) insertions and \(d(d-1)d!\) gain comparisons. Memoization uses at most \(d2^{d-1}\) conditional-risk queries and \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC queries, followed by at most \(d(d-1)/2\) pruning checks.
proposed.justification: The primitive certificate is useful only if it yields a complete labelled-DAG recovery theorem and a finite oracle budget.
proposed.gap: Solus, Wang, and Uhler (2021, Proposition 8 and Theorem 9) study covered-arrow walks for sparsity, while Li et al. (2025) do not give primitive risk and dependence query counts for GENE.
proposed.consumer: An implementation can cache the finite local-score table and know its worst-case population-query budget.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the matching-component and characteristic-kernel premises used directly by the pruning proof.
